Aiming, camera and on-screen feedback

This guide explains what the screen tells you while you move and aim, and the camera settings that change how movement feels.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 5 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Read the crosshair
  2. Steady ranged aim
  3. Read the looking-at card
  4. Status line and pickups

Read the crosshair

The plus-shaped crosshair marks where your aim lands. It inverts the colours under it, so it stays readable over sky, grass and stone. It is hidden in the front third-person view. Crosshair and aiming reticle

  • With a bow, rifle or throwable in hand, the four lines spread apart as your accuracy drops. They close back into a plus as your aim steadies.
  • Other items keep the closed plus.

Steady ranged aim

The spread of a bow, rifle or throwable depends on how you stand, move and shoot. Steadier aim for ranged weapons

Key or actionWhat it does
Hold Shift (crouch)Tightens the spread.
Moving on footWidens the spread. Faster movement widens it more.
In the airWidens the spread.
Bow drawA fuller draw steadies the aim.
Rifle sightsRaising the rifle's sights steadies the aim.
Each shotBriefly opens the reticle.

Read the looking-at card

When you aim at a block within 6 m, a card at the top right of the screen shows it. The card sits just left of the compact map. Looking-at card (F2)

  • The card shows the block's 3D icon, name and distance.
  • The mining advice is one of: "CREATIVE INSTANT BREAK", the recommended tool, or "NO SPECIAL TOOL NEEDED".
  • An animal gets its own card, with its health.
Key or actionWhat it does
F2Hide or show the card in the world.
Settings > General > TARGET INFO (F2)The same setting. It is saved with each world.
Tip. The card is hidden while a menu is open.

Status line and pickups

Actions report in the status line at the top left. Status line, pickup and damage feedback

  • Mining reports "Collected <block> x<pieces>". Pieces go straight into your pack.
  • A full pack says "Capacity full; block left behind". The block stays in the world.
  • Opening your pack says "Inventory opened".
  • Mined blocks throw debris and play a break sound. Dropped items are not on the ground yet.
Good to know. Taking damage has no hurt sound and no red flash. The camera dip is the only cue. See the camera section below.

Camera bob, speed view and damage dip

Three camera effects change how movement and hits feel. Each has a row in Settings > General. Camera bob and speed field of view

Key or actionWhat it does
CAMERA BOBWalking gently bobs the camera. Turn it off here.
SPEED FOVOff or On. On widens the view by up to 5 degrees at high horizontal speed, reaching full widening at about 16 m/s. Jumps and falls do not change it.
DAMAGE BOBOff, Reduced or Full. Full is the default. After a hit of at least 1 HP, the camera dips up to 7 cm at Full and half that at Reduced.
  • Speed FOV eases over about 0.3 s, so a sprint-jump does not pump the view.
  • Vehicles have their own speed effect, which the SPEED FOV row also turns off.
  • Only real health loss causes the dip. Hunger, cold, respawn and loading do not.
  • The dip does not move what you aim at. Aiming and interaction still use your eye position.

Collection feed (survival)

In survival, a small feed in the lower-right corner lists what you gained, for example "+3 Oak wood". Lower-right collection feed

  • Gains come from mined blocks, felled trees, hunted animals, filled flasks, exploration finds and packed boats or homes.
  • A gain of an item that is already listed adds to its row.
  • Up to five rows show. Each stays for about 4 seconds and fades over its last 0.8 s.
  • Creative mining, crafting, the creative catalog, home storage and loading a save show nothing.

Water sounds and splashes

Water entry splashes and bubbles

  • Stepping or falling into water plays a splash sound and throws droplets from the surface.
  • Moving through water releases bubbles and a swim sound about every 1.4 m.
  • Rain makes small ripple splashes on surfaces.
  • Boats leave no bow spray or wake.

Held items and the character portrait

A block you select is shown as a small textured cube in your right hand. Tools are held on the right, and the bow sits left of centre with its own string hand. With nothing in hand, or with a block you no longer carry in survival, your bare right arm rests low on the right. Hold left click to swing a tool, bare hand or held block; bows and rifles do not swing. Placing a block plays one swing. The swing is visual only. A held sailing boat shows no hand. F1 hides held items in the clean view. Held blocks and hands (first person)

Press E, stay on Pack and click Character to see a 3D portrait of your explorer. Move the pointer across it to turn the model. It shows Creative or your health, and what you are holding. There are no appearance, outfit or skin options. Remote players in multiplayer use the same fixed explorer model. Character tab (portrait only)

How this guide was checked

Crosshair spread, aim steadiness, the looking-at card, the status line, camera effects, the collection feed and water effects come from the feature ledger, which cites Voxelgame source lines. The numbers were rechecked at Voxelgame commit 0494a0ce: 6 m target reach, Speed FOV 5 degrees reaching full at 16 m/s with a 0.3 s ease, a 7 cm damage dip on hits of at least 1 HP, 5 feed rows shown for 4 s with a 0.8 s fade, and 14 splash droplets.

Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; guide written 12 October 2026. Source-checked, not play-tested, and without screenshots. Judge the bob and dip strength in play. Spread amounts are internal values, so the guide describes their direction rather than exact degrees. Features covered, with their source evidence: Crosshair and aiming reticle, Steadier aim for ranged weapons, Looking-at card (F2), Status line, pickup and damage feedback, Camera bob and speed field of view, Lower-right collection feed, Water entry splashes and bubbles, Held blocks and hands (first person), Character tab (portrait only).
